interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 8.7 and an ISUP grade group 3 Gleason pattern on prostatectomy. Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension and no seminal vesicle invasion documented in the surgical pathology report. The positive surgical margins are concerning for local recurrence risk. Notably, there is no nodal status reported as nodes were not removed, which widens uncertainty regarding nodal involvement. Furthermore, the biopsy history shows a discrepancy, with the second biopsy identifying Gleason 3+4 compared to the prostatectomy grade of Gleason 4+3. The trajectory of postoperative PSA and subsequent follow-up data would significantly revise this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 56.82 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 36.93–76.70 months; its coverage has not been validated.
